builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
summary: ARISE replaces manual prompt and workflow refinement after agent failures with an automated loop that attributes failures, stores corrections as retrievable micro memories, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts rule updates only when held-out accuracy improves, all without changing model weights, tools, or workflow logic. It costs extra attribution and consolidation calls (optionally to a stronger teacher model such as Claude Opus), a memory store with retrieval added to each inference, and the engineering of an evaluation gate, though it slightly reduces model calls and output tokens at deployment. It can fail if the self- or teacher-attribution misdiagnoses errors and pollutes memory with harmful rules, if the held-out set is unrepresentative so accepted rules do not generalize, or if retrieved memories degrade as workflows and underlying models change.
rationale: The method requires no weight updates or infrastructure beyond API access and a retrieval store, but its gains depend on reliable failure attribution and a held-out acceptance loop, so the reader should validate it on their own workflow before production adoption.
technique: Self-evolving failure-attribution memory for LLM agents

It costs extra attribution and consolidation calls (optionally to a stronger teacher model such as Claude Opus), a memory store with retrieval added to each inference, and the engineering of an evaluation gate, though it slightly reduces model calls and output tokens at deployment. It can fail if the self- or teacher-attribution misdiagnoses errors and pollutes memory with harmful rules, if the held-out set is unrepresentative so accepted rules do not generalize, or if retrieved memories degrade as workflows and underlying models change.

ARISE-Teacher gains 10.9 pp over baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on tau2-bench; ARISE-Self gains 10.0 pp on SOP-Bench, with 4.0% fewer model calls and 5.2% fewer output tokens at comparable per-task cost.
